title: XOR with the all-zeros vector
statement: For every $x \in \{0,1\}^n$, the componentwise XOR of $x$ with the all-zeros vector $\mathbf{0}$ equals $x$; that is, $x \oplus \mathbf{0} = x$. Equivalently, $\mathbf{0}$ is a right identity for the group operation on $(\bbf_2)^n$.
hypotheses_covered: x is a point of the Boolean hypercube {0,1}^n
replaced:
For all $x \in \{0,1\}^n$, we have $x \oplus \mathbf{0} = x$, where
$\mathbf{0}$ denotes the all-zero vector.
